purpose: Decision rules fixed on development data BEFORE the data that tests them exist. The git commit that adds a rule is its registration timestamp; scripts/benchmark.py aggregate reads the rule from this file and never re-fits it.

pipeline_selective.description: Answer with the pipeline's route only when its own retrieval evidence is strong; otherwise abstain to city level, i.e. answer with the geocoded centre of the --city string (the city_centroid baseline). The question it tests: does the pipeline know when it is wrong?
pipeline_selective.signal_rule: the first of these present in result.json is the confidence (median top-1 cosine similarity between the query frames and their retrieved street-level images); a run with neither (retrieval absent or skipped) abstains

derivation.data: run v2, core fleet, 18 reps (6 clips x 3); package code 18e65ae (Ulm 4K rep0: 4747814, same package tree)
derivation.label: a rep is a WIN when the pipeline's symmetric error is below the city-centroid guess's, a LOSS otherwise

no_signal.ulm2: coarse-to-fine did not run (a one-word title seed set an 800 m gate), so no confidence was recorded; the rule abstains (LOSS in all 3 reps: 7662 m vs 350 m)

derivation.procedure: tau = midpoint between the highest LOSS confidence (0.1298) and the lowest WIN confidence (0.1939) = 0.1619, rounded to 0.162. One free parameter; nothing else was tuned. The dev data separate perfectly, so dev performance says nothing about generalisation; only the held-out test does.

held_out_test.data: run v2, overlay fleet (9 clips in 5 US/UK cities; ground truth from the GPS stamp burned into the dashcam video); none of these clips was used to choose tau
held_out_test.code: package code 4fda123 (pipeline decomposed into monocular_osm/stages/ and an off-by-default --graph-filter added since 18e65ae; behaviour preservation checked by scripts/golden_pipeline.py)
held_out_test.disclosure: Before registration one overlay log line had been seen: overlay_vCSEG6KaFng rep2, coarse-to-fine pass-2 similarity 0.131 (below tau). No overlay localisation error had been seen; overlay reps 0 and 1 of that clip had crashed on a full disk without producing a result. An earlier note in the working session gave tau ~0.17 from rep0 values only; this file's 0.162 comes from all 18 reps by the procedure above, and the difference does not change the decision for the one overlay value seen.

hypotheses.H1: Per clip (median over reps, symmetric error), pipeline_selective beats the pipeline on more overlay clips than it loses to it (sign test over clips, ties excluded).
hypotheses.H2: Among overlay clips where pipeline_selective answers (does not abstain), the pipeline beats the city-centroid guess on a majority.
hypotheses.H3: Overlay reps with confidence >= tau beat the city-centroid guess more often than reps below tau (one-sided Fisher exact test over reps).

held_out_test.power_note: About 9 held-out clips: only large effects are detectable, and a null result is not evidence of no effect. The result is reported whichever way it comes out.

safevpr_frame_verification.description: Does a calibrated accept/abstain decision on retrieval keep its error rate on footage it was not calibrated on? SafeVPR (Sier et al., arXiv 2605.28048, MIT, code f11d5fd) verifies a retrieval with DINOv2 ViT-L/14 patch mutual-nearest-neighbour + Lowe-ratio matching and calibrates a per-score-bin threshold with Mondrian Learn-Then-Test; the tau rule above (a single cosine threshold) did not transfer from the core to the overlay clips.
safevpr_frame_verification.unit: one query frame and the MegaLoc top-1 reference of the first (city-disc) retrieval pass: the 80 query frames the pipeline samples over the analysis window, against the exact reference set benchmark run v2 searched (rep0, archived)
safevpr_frame_verification.label: correct iff the top-1 reference lies within 50 m of the ground truth interpolated at the query's video time

scores.patch_mnn: safevpr.verifier: extract_patch_features + mnn_lowe_ratio on the (query, top-1 reference) pair, i.e. verify_pair with T=1 (our references are single photos, not sequences); paper constants unchanged (224x224, ratio 0.9)

safevpr_frame_verification.calibration: safevpr.conformal.fit_mondrian_ltt at alpha = 0.10 (paper defaults: 5 bins, delta 0.05), fitted once per score on the core clips (dev), never on the overlay clips
safevpr_frame_verification.test: the nine overlay clips (v2 rep0 each)

hypotheses.S1: With the patch_mnn score, the empirical false-discovery rate among accepted overlay frames is <= 0.10.
hypotheses.S2: With the cosine score calibrated the same way, the overlay FDR is higher than with patch_mnn (or cosine accepts none while patch_mnn accepts some at FDR <= 0.10).
hypotheses.S3: On the overlay frames the AUROC of patch_mnn for correct vs wrong exceeds that of cosine.

safevpr_frame_verification.disclosure: The overlay clips were the held-out test of the tau rule and their titles were read when writing the title-seed rule; no overlay per-frame retrieval label, cosine or verifier score had been computed when this was registered. Few frames are correct at 50 m (on Ulm 4K, 7 % of pass-1 top-1 retrievals), so acceptance may be very low; that is reported, not changed.
safevpr_frame_verification.power_note: ~480 calibration and ~720 test frames, but frames of one clip are not independent; results are also reported per clip.

graph_filter_dashcam.description: Does the retrieval-free road-graph particle filter with road-plane speed (localized KITTI 0033 city-wide in 5/5 seeds) work on dashcam footage? The pipeline's failures trace to retrieval reference coverage; this channel needs no references.
graph_filter_dashcam.method: the --graph-filter defaults at commit 3ab1b5a: monocular_osm.plane_speed with an assumed 1.5 m camera height on the frames the cached VO used (same stride and window, downscaled to 960 px wide with the intrinsics scaled to match), VO rotation heading, FilterConfig(metric_logk_sigma=0.25, metric_speed_dev_sigma=clip(estimator spread, 0.05, 0.3)), 600,000 particles, 2 Hz, 3 seeds. Nothing tuned on these clips.
graph_filter_dashcam.map: the clip's deployable search disc: the drive network within the pipeline's city-extent radius (text_anchor.city_extent_radius, clipped to 3-8 km) around the geocoded centre of the manifest city string; a route outside it cannot be localized by construction and is reported as such
graph_filter_dashcam.clips: every manifest clip with a cached VO trajectory (core YouTube clips, KITTI excluded as already reported, and the nine overlay clips)
graph_filter_dashcam.outcome: per clip, the symmetric error (metrics.score_route) of the filter's smoothed route, median over seeds, against ground truth; a clip is localized when the median final error is < 50 m
graph_filter_dashcam.comparison: per clip against the pipeline's symmetric error in the latest run with the same code fixes (v3 for core clips, v4 for overlay clips); sign test over clips, ties excluded

hypotheses.G1: The filter localizes at least one dashcam clip (median final error < 50 m).
hypotheses.G2: The filter's smoothed-route error beats the pipeline's on more clips than it loses (sign test).

graph_filter_dashcam.disclosure: The road-plane estimator and the filter settings were developed on KITTI 0009/0033 only; the dashcam clips' ground truth has been used to score the pipeline before, never for the filter or the speed estimator. Speed accuracy on dashcam footage is unknown and is reported against the ground-truth timing (exploratory).

seed_ring.description: Does searching a sparse reference ring out to the seed's own radius (--vpr-seed-ring) fix seeded clips whose route lies outside the 3 km retrieval core, without breaking seeded clips that already work?
seed_ring.method: --vpr-seed-ring at the commit that adds it: when a coarse seed (title place names, plate district) is wider than vpr_search_radius_m (3 km), pass 1 also lists the seed disc out to min(seed radius, 8 km) with the city-extent mode's ref cap (1,200 with a token) in its own cache, minus the core ids; the 3 km/1,500 core set, pass 2 and everything downstream are unchanged. Motivated by the v3/v4 archives (route inside the 3 km core: Atlanta kxED 0 %, KITTI 0033 0 %, Berlin 38 %), flagged as an open structural issue in docs/experiments_2026-10.md section 1 before any ring result existed. No constant is new or tuned.
seed_ring.clips: dev clips whose run log shows a coarse seed wider than 3 km: berlin_0-420, london, ulm2, kitti_0033, overlay_Wrn4_uCxRCQ, overlay_kxEDNj5L_yQ (other clips never take the ring branch). One cold rep each, run v7 = v6 code + --vpr-seed-ring.
seed_ring.outcome: symmetric_mean_m per clip (benchmark aggregate), v7 against v6 on the same clips

hypotheses.S1: No clip with symmetric error <= 200 m in v5 is above 200 m in v6 (no harm to working clips).
hypotheses.S2: At least one clip above 200 m in v5 is at or below 200 m in v6, OR the ring improves more clips than it worsens (changes under 10 % of the v5 error count as ties).

seed_ring.decision: Make --vpr-seed-ring the default iff S1 and S2 both hold; otherwise leave it off and report the result either way. The held-out test split is scored only after this decision, with whatever default results.
seed_ring.disclosure: Single cold rep per clip; earlier repeated cold runs differed by tens to hundreds of metres on some clips, so a one-rep result near a threshold is weak evidence and is reported as such.

amendments.reason: v5 (Graph API listing with tile splitting) was stopped after 5 clips when the Graph bbox search proved to truncate silently even without errors (Karlsruhe: 498,876 listed vs 836,869 in Mapillary's coverage tiles). The listing now reads coverage tiles; v6 measures that on every dev clip, and the ring must be compared against the same listing. No seed-ring run or result existed at the time of this amendment.

outcome_recorded.S1: holds (London and Ulm #2, the clips within 200 m in v6, unchanged)
outcome_recorded.S2: fails (no clip crosses to within 200 m; 1 improved, 1 worsened, 4 ties)
outcome_recorded.decision: not adopted: --vpr-seed-ring stays off by default

test_split_2026_10.method: the pipeline's defaults at the first commit after the seed_ring decision is recorded (whatever that decision is), run by scripts/benchmark.py run --split test --cold-vpr, one rep per clip, MLY_TOKEN set, the same runner settings as v5; the commit is recorded in the run's run_config.json. No code, constant or default changes between seeing any test result and reporting all of them.
test_split_2026_10.outcome: symmetric_mean_m per clip (benchmark aggregate, the same metric as the dev runs), plus final-position error

hypotheses.T2: The share of test clips at or under 200 m is reported with a Wilson 95 % interval next to the same share on the dev clips in the latest dev run; no threshold is claimed in advance.

answer_selection.description: Which route the method answers with: the trajectory fit (the pipeline's result.position), the retrieval track itself, or the fit checked against the track. Prompted by v6, where the smoothed retrieval track scored better than the fit on 3 of the first 5 dev clips.

candidates.P: the pipeline's headline route (result.position), as before
candidates.T: the retrieval track as a route: result.vpr_prior.track in time order, each point the running median of 5 (lat and lon separately); monocular_osm.baselines.vpr_track_only
candidates.C: P, unless its disagreement with the track exceeds D = 250 m, then T. Disagreement = median over the smoothed track points of the distance to the nearest point of P's route. D is the benchmark's existing 250 m success threshold, fixed here before any disagreement value was computed.

answer_selection.selection: on the dev clips of v6 (with v7 in place of v6 for the seeded clips if seed_ring is adopted), choose the candidate with the most clips at symmetric error <= 200 m; ties broken by the lower median symmetric error over those clips; a remaining tie keeps P. Candidates that need the track (T, C) fall back to P on a run without one.
answer_selection.use: the selected candidate is the method's answer on the test split (rule test_split_2026_10, whose T1/T2 then refer to it); the other two are reported alongside.
answer_selection.disclosure: Seen before registration (v6, symmetric error, P / T): Berlin 695 / 135, KITTI 0009 3,608 / 3,735, London 22 / 63, Ulm #2 106 / 46, Ulm 4K 36 / 15. Nothing else of v6, and no value of C, had been computed. The other ten dev clips of v6 were still running.

outcome_recorded.decision: T selected: the method answers with the retrieval track (--answer track is the default from the commit recording this)

metro_ring_dev_2026_11.description: Development check, before any run of it: does searching the city's surroundings when the retrieval track is weak (--vpr-metro-ring) recover routes that lie outside the searched disc, without breaking clips that already work? All three used splits serve as development data here; a held-out claim needs the third split (test3), registered separately once the method is frozen.
metro_ring_dev_2026_11.method: --vpr-metro-ring --retrieval-only (answer: the retrieval track) at the commit that adds it. When the selective rule's confidence (vpr_coarse_to_fine.pass2_sim, else the track's median cosine) is below its pre-registered tau 0.162, the run covers the disc of 20 km around the city's geocode minus the disc pass 1 searched with 4 km hex cells, each with the pass-1 city disc's reference density (300 refs with a token), densifies up to 3 supported cells (1,500 refs), lets the existing regional continuity merge choose between them and the ordinary track, and, if ring evidence is selected, refines with a coarse-to-fine pass at the new centre under the ordinary pass-2 margin (0.02). Above tau nothing changes.
metro_ring_dev_2026_11.constants: tau, the cell hierarchy, its fine budget and the pass-2 margin are reused unchanged; the 4 km cell radius and 300-ref cap follow from the pass-1 density (1,200 refs per 8 km disc). The 20 km outer radius was chosen after seeing the used splits' ground truth: the six mode-A failures lie 10.8-16.8 km (median route point) from the city geocode (docs/failure_taxonomy_2026-11.md); it is not tuned on any metro-ring result.
metro_ring_dev_2026_11.clips: all 29 scored clips of the used splits: dev (15), test (7), test2 (7). The gate is decided by each run itself; 15 clips were below tau in their frozen runs.
metro_ring_dev_2026_11.run: one rep per clip, CPU retrieval, --skip-download, a clean worktree at the method commit, data copies holding the frozen runs' inputs and warm ordinary-retrieval caches (ring caches start cold)
metro_ring_dev_2026_11.outcome: per clip, the symmetric_mean_m of the answer with the ring against the same run's ordinary track (recorded before the ring step as metro_ring_retrieval.baseline_track and scored identically: running median of 5, monocular_osm.metrics.score_route); wall-clock time per clip

hypotheses.M1: No clip whose ordinary track is within 200 m is above 200 m with the ring (no harm).
hypotheses.M2: At least two clips above 200 m with the ordinary track are within 200 m with the ring, and the ring improves more clips than it worsens (changes under 10 % are ties).

metro_ring_dev_2026_11.decision: If M1 and M2 hold, the method is frozen at that commit and compared with the frozen track method on test3 under a separate rule registered before any test3 run; otherwise it is not taken to test3 as is, and the result is reported either way.
metro_ring_dev_2026_11.disclosure: In-sample by construction (the outer radius used these clips' ground truth). One rep per clip; earlier repeated cold runs of the same clip differed by tens to hundreds of metres, and a rerun may land on the other side of tau.
